headline: The family is THREE different things in a 4/4/4 split. That is why reports/c68 recorded 'no decisive signature' and reports/c75 declined to re-bucket it -- the label was never a shape.

A_capped_lethal_cascade.signature: both sides carry capped_lethal and the NETS AGREE EXACTLY (e.g. -125 + -40 = -133 + -32 = -165; -45 + -67 = -47 + -65 = -112)
A_capped_lethal_cascade.the_reference: a residual that kills is clipped to whatever HP remains. Each arm clips to ITS OWN remaining HP, so the arm that took LESS direct damage has MORE left and its cap is LARGER. Conservation is exact.
A_capped_lethal_cascade.the_matcher: scripts/engine_transition_differential.py, the capped_lethal branch of roll_components_agree (~line 809), tests `abs(obs) <= abs(eng) + 1`. Its comment says the capped value 'can only ever be SMALLER than the uncapped tick the engine carries -- here the one-sided inequality IS the sound test'. That is true only when ONE side is capped. When BOTH are, the direction is set by which arm took less damage, and the observed cap is legitimately the larger one. 19000002/61: |obs| 40 > |eng| 32 + 1, so it rejects a pair that conserves exactly.
A_capped_lethal_cascade.disposition: MATCHER FIX. The exact mirror of the capped-HEAL cascade #1025 addresses: two caps differ by precisely the direct-damage difference, in the opposite direction. Needs the same difference bound, and a pin that fails when the one-sided test is restored.
A_capped_lethal_cascade.why_not_an_engine_gap: the engine's arm is a legal roll and its capped_lethal is correctly clipped. Nothing is missing from the support.

B_lethality_disagreement.signature: one side kills and the other does not; the nets differ (obs -100 vs eng -107 + capped_lethal -11 = -118)
B_lethality_disagreement.reading: the engine's arm KO'd where the observation did not, or the reverse. This looks like the same class as limit:roll_divergent_lethality, which is already adjudicated as a comparison limit.
B_lethality_disagreement.disposition: NOT YET DETERMINED. The deciding question is whether the OBSERVED outcome is present in the engine's branch SET. If a non-killing arm exists and simply lost the majority, it is a branch-selection/comparison limit. If no arm reproduces the observation, it is an engine gap. That check is the next step and has not been run.

C_component_absent_from_the_engine.signature: the observation carries a component the engine emits nothing for -- abilityroughskin -16 vs [], +24 vs +23, +17 vs [], -24 vs []
C_component_absent_from_the_engine.reading: at least one (19000021/34, Rough Skin) is an ability the engine does not model on that path -- an engine gap. The +24/+23 row is a magnitude difference, not an absence, and does not belong with the other three.
C_component_absent_from_the_engine.disposition: NOT YET DETERMINED. Needs per-row source comparison; these are probably 2-3 further distinct causes.

what_this_establishes: 12 rows resolve into 4 with a stated matcher cause and disposition, and 8 that need further per-row source work but are now separated into two clearly different questions rather than one opaque family. The 'candidate-not-finding' label was hiding a partition, not a hard problem.
method_note: This took one classification pass over the retained repros plus reading two functions. No new instrumentation. c75 concluded these families needed 'evidence the current signatures do not measure' -- true of SIGNATURE profiling, and not true of reading the rows.
